overview: The Department of Home Affairs is responsible for civic services including identity documents, passports, birth and death registration, marriages, and citizenship. It is one of the most-used and most-frustrating government services for South Africans.

services.name: Smart ID Card (First Issue)
services.description: The Smart ID card replaces the old green bar-coded ID book. All South Africans 16 and older should have one.
requirements: South African birth certificate (unabridged preferred)
If 16: parent/guardian must accompany with their own ID
Proof of address (utility bill, lease, affidavit)
If applicable: marriage certificate, divorce decree
process: Visit your nearest Home Affairs office
Complete the BI-9 application form (available at the office)
Your fingerprints and photograph will be taken digitally
You will receive a receipt with a reference number — KEEP THIS
Collection is from the same office where you applied
Processing time: officially 1-3 months, but frequently takes 6-12 months
common_problems: Application 'stuck' in the system for months — use the reference number to follow up
Office says 'system is offline' — this is common, ask when to return or try another office
Fingerprints rejected by the system — request manual override or try at a different office
ID allocated to wrong person — escalate immediately, this is an identity fraud risk
services.tracking: Check status at www.dha.gov.za/index.php/id-status or call 0800 60 11 90

services.name: Smart ID Card (Replacement)
requirements: Affidavit explaining loss/theft (from SAPS)
Any available identification (old ID, passport, driver's license)
Proof of address
process: Obtain affidavit from nearest police station
Visit Home Affairs with affidavit and any ID you have
Pay R140 fee
Fingerprints and photo retaken
Same processing time as first issue

services.name: Passport
requirements: Valid Smart ID card (you cannot apply with the old green ID book)
Completed BI-73 application form
Proof of address
If child: both parents' IDs, consent from both parents (or court order if single parent)
process: Visit Home Affairs or selected bank branches (Nedbank, Standard Bank, FNB)
Complete form, have biometrics taken
Pay the fee
Processing time: 4-6 weeks (standard), 48 hours (emergency — R800 extra)
Collect from the office where you applied
common_problems: Cannot apply without Smart ID — you must get the Smart ID first
Passport takes longer than 6 weeks — escalate to the office manager
Child passport refused due to missing parent consent — get a court order from the Family Court

services.name: Birth Certificate (Registration of Birth)
services.description: All births must be registered within 30 days. Late registration (after 30 days) requires additional documentation.

requirements: Notification of Birth form (completed by the hospital/midwife)
Both parents' IDs (or mother's ID if father is unknown/absent)
If parents are married: marriage certificate
process: Visit Home Affairs within 30 days of birth
Submit the Notification of Birth form
Birth certificate is usually issued same day or within a few days

requirements: Sworn affidavit explaining why registration is late
Baptismal certificate or school records as proof of birth
Both parents' IDs
Hospital records if available
process: Visit Home Affairs with all available documentation
Complete the late registration form
Home Affairs may conduct an investigation
Processing can take 3-6 months for late registrations

services.name: Death Certificate
requirements: Notification of Death form (BI-1663) completed by a medical practitioner
Deceased's ID document
Informant's ID (the person reporting the death)
process: Death must be registered within 72 hours
Visit Home Affairs with the completed BI-1663 form
Submit the deceased's ID (it will be cancelled)
An abridged death certificate is issued immediately
Unabridged death certificate takes 6-8 weeks

services.name: Marriage Registration
requirements: Both parties must be 18 or older (or have parental consent if under 18)
Both parties' ID documents
If previously married: decree of divorce or death certificate of former spouse
Two witnesses with their IDs
services.civil_marriage: Performed at Home Affairs offices. Book at least 3 months in advance.
services.customary_marriage: Must be registered at Home Affairs within 3 months of the ceremony. Bring letter from family/community confirming the marriage.

bank_branch_services: Standard Bank, FNB, and Nedbank selected branches offer Smart ID and passport applications
These are usually faster with shorter queues — but not all services are available
Check the DHA website for a list of participating bank branches

escalation.step_1: Ask to speak with the office manager at the branch where you applied
escalation.step_2: Contact the Provincial Manager for KwaZulu-Natal via the DHA call centre
escalation.step_3: Lodge a formal complaint via the Presidential Hotline: 17737
escalation.step_4: Lodge a complaint with the Public Protector: 0800 11 20 40
escalation.step_5: As a last resort, approach the High Court for a mandamus order compelling Home Affairs to process your application
escalation.legislation: The Identification Act 68 of 1997 and the Births and Deaths Registration Act 51 of 1992 govern these services. Unreasonable delays can be challenged under Section 33 of the Constitution (right to just administrative action) and the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act (PAJA).

your_rights: Section 28(1)(a) of the Constitution: every child has the right to a name and nationality from birth
Section 33: everyone has the right to administrative action that is lawful, reasonable, and procedurally fair
Home Affairs must process ID applications within a reasonable time — courts have found 3+ months unreasonable
You cannot be denied service because of system downtime — the office must record your details and process when systems restore
You may not be asked to pay a bribe or 'speed up' fee — report this immediately
